Open a gRPC channel

Source: R/channel.R
grpc_channel.Rd

A channel holds what every call to one server shares: the server's address, the headers sent on every call, the message size limit, and the zuhttp client whose connection pool carries the calls. An http:// URL speaks cleartext HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c), for a local server. An https:// URL negotiates HTTP/2 over TLS. gRPC has no HTTP/1.1 fallback, so the channel's client always requires HTTP/2.

Usage

grpc_channel(
  url,
  headers = NULL,
  tls = NULL,
  max_message = 128 * 1024^2,
  client = NULL
)

Arguments

url

The server, as http://host:port or https://host:port. No path, query or user information.

headers

Metadata sent on every call: a named character vector or a named list, as metadata in grpc_call(). A call's own metadata replaces a channel header of the same name.

tls

Certificate trust settings from zuhttp::zu_tls(), for an https:// URL.

max_message

The largest response message accepted, in bytes. The default, 128 MiB, is Spark Connect's. A larger message fails the call with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

client

A zuhttp::zu_client() to build on, so that proxies, TLS pins, middleware and test transports come from zuhttp unchanged. The channel derives its own client from it, with HTTP/2 required. NULL builds a fresh one.

Value

A zugrpc_channel.

See also

grpc_call() to make a call, grpc_close() to close it.

Examples

ch <- grpc_channel("http://localhost:50051")
ch
#> <zugrpc_channel> localhost:50051
#>   transport: cleartext HTTP/2 (h2c)
#>   state:     open
#>   streams:   0 open
grpc_close(ch)
